nodes.label: Four-Service Compose Stack
nodes.rationale: db, api, worker, web under Compose Spec syntax. No Redis and no broker: the cache and the job queue are both Postgres.

nodes.label: Per-Service Resource Ceilings
nodes.rationale: 1 GiB db, 512 MB api, 2 GiB worker, 256 MB web. Lapidary must run on a modest workstation, not only on a machine with spare gigabytes; the worker gets the largest share because it is the only service that parses meshes, and this ceiling is what makes deferring the L1/L2 rungs a memory decision rather than a latency one.

nodes.label: SERVER_FEATURES Build-Time Image Split
nodes.rationale: One Containerfile builds both images; only worker sets SERVER_FEATURES: mock-kernel, so the api image never links the CAD kernel at all. api logs kernel=none, worker logs kernel=mock. LAPIDARY_ROLE must never be 'api' on the worker — see lapidary-api::Role and ApiError::UnknownRole.

nodes.label: Storage Root As A Bind-Mounted Host Directory
nodes.rationale: A named volume the user cannot locate on disk would defeat the whole point of the browsable layout. Mounted read-write on api too, which is not a hole in the open-path rule: that boundary is a type — SourceStore demands a WorkerRole token lapidary-api cannot obtain — not a mount flag, and a read-only mount would break the derivative cache writes and the upload commit the api legitimately needs.

nodes.label: Uploads Volume Outside The Storage Root
nodes.rationale: Chunks in flight get their own named volume, deliberately not a subdirectory of LAPIDARY_BLOB_ROOT: everything under that root is content-addressed and complete, and a half-transferred file is neither. Persistent on purpose, because the staged file's length is what a resuming upload asks for, so an api restart costs nothing instead of a re-transfer.

nodes.label: Mount The Postgres Parent, Not .../data
nodes.rationale: From PostgreSQL 18 the official image stores data in a major-version-scoped subdirectory, so mounting the old /var/lib/postgresql/data makes the entrypoint hard-fail. Mounting the parent is upstream's recommendation and allows pg_upgrade --link later. Consequence: moving to PG19 is a pg_upgrade job, not a tag change.

nodes.label: Lowercase z, Not Z, On User Directories
nodes.rationale: On an SELinux-enforcing host an unlabelled bind mount gets the worker EACCES on every file. `Z` takes a private per-container label of a directory that belongs to the user and may be open in other programs; `z` applies a shared label, which is what a directory that remains theirs wants. Only lapidary-db is still a named volume.

nodes.label: Empty Worker Knobs Mean 'Use The Default'
nodes.rationale: Defaults live in lapidary_jobs::WorkerConfig so exactly one place decides them; restating the numbers in compose would let the two drift. ${VAR:-} yields a present-but-empty variable for every operator who never set one, and an empty string is not a usize — empty_str_as_none in bin/lapidary-server/src/main.rs exists so that case starts the worker instead of refusing to boot.
